tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Ironvale Manufacturing** produces industrial sensors and operates two factories and a head office. The company runs Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) on-premises and has recently purchased Microsoft 365 subscriptions for all 1,200 employees.

**Current Environment:**
- All user accounts are created and managed in on-premises AD DS.
- Employees currently maintain a separate password for the new cloud services.
- About 80 external contractors help with seasonal production planning and sign in from outside the company network.
- A small IT team of five administrators holds permanent, highly privileged directory roles.

tabs.title: Identity Requirements
tabs.content:
Ironvale Manufacturing has defined the following requirements for its identity platform:
- **Single set of credentials**: Employees must sign in to Microsoft 365 with the same password they use on-premises, with the least possible additional server infrastructure. Cloud sign-in must keep working even if the on-premises network is unavailable.
- **Risk-appropriate authentication**: Contractors must be prompted for multifactor authentication only when they sign in from outside the corporate network; employees on the factory floor should not receive unnecessary prompts.
- **Reduce standing privilege**: Administrators should receive privileged directory roles only when needed, for a limited time, and with an approval step and an audit trail.
